sentences.text: The River Intake Pump Station normally operates in automatic service, with pump starts governed by raw-water demand and available channel depth.
Reduced-capacity service is used when river level, equipment condition, or downstream process demand does not support full intake operation.
Storm Intake Mode is used when rainfall, river rise, debris loading, or upstream runoff creates conditions that require closer supervision of the intake.
The Chief Operator authorizes entry into Storm Intake Mode when field observations or instrument trends show that normal assumptions are no longer reliable.
During Storm Intake Mode, plant staff increase observation of river level, screen loading, turbidity, and pump cycling frequency.
The Raw Water Screen Channel is monitored for upstream level, downstream level, differential level, rake run status, and high-debris indications.
A rising differential level across the Raw Water Screen Channel is treated as an early indication of screen blinding or heavy floating debris.
The Raw Water Screen Channel sends the Rake Torque Snapshot at the end of each cleaning cycle to preserve the recorded loading condition.
If the Raw Water Screen Channel shows rapid level change, plant staff verify that the cleaning mechanism is running and that the River Intake Pump Station is not drawing the channel down too quickly.
A high-high level condition at the Raw Water Screen Channel requires immediate field confirmation because it may indicate restricted passage, failed cleaning, or abnormal river backwater.
Raw-water quality triggers include high turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints from field staff, visible sheen, algae accumulation, and rapid temperature change.
When a raw-water quality trigger occurs, the Chief Operator determines whether to adjust pumping rate, request additional laboratory testing, or increase downstream process monitoring.
The Laboratory Technician supports intake decisions by prioritizing raw-water checks when storm runoff or an abnormal visual condition is reported.
The Coagulant Dosing Skid is placed under closer observation when intake turbidity changes faster than the normal control response can stabilize.
The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are advised when incoming water quality is expected to shorten filter run time or increase solids loading.
Pump permissives at the River Intake Pump Station include adequate suction level, available discharge path, healthy motor status, open isolation valves, and absence of active protective trips.
A pump is not permitted to start when the Raw Water Screen Channel downstream level is below the established low-level limit.
A pump start is also blocked when the associated drive reports a fault, when local control is selected, or when a safety interlock is not proven.
If a permissive is lost during operation, the control system either alarms the condition or stops the affected pump according to the severity of the signal.
The Chief Operator may authorize temporary manual operation only when the cause is understood, the equipment can be observed, and the risk to treatment continuity is acceptable.
The SCADA Historian Server retains river level, screen differential, pump status, and raw-water quality trends for operating review and event reconstruction.
The Duty Engineer reviews storm forecasts and river-stage information when a prolonged debris event or high-flow period is expected.
The Distribution Dispatcher is notified when intake limitations could reduce the ability of the High Service Pump Header to meet planned system demand.
The Clearwell Level Controller is watched during intake restrictions because storage level provides the main buffer between reduced raw-water supply and treated-water delivery.
Return to normal service occurs after river level, screen differential, raw-water quality, and pump cycling have stabilized for a period accepted by the Chief Operator.
After a storm event, the Maintenance Planner reviews intake equipment condition and schedules cleaning or inspection work needed to restore reliable operation.
